relation_types.team_continuation: One paper cites another and shares a non-common exact author name; this is a team-continuation signal, not a technical-lineage assertion.
relation_types.affiliated_with: An organization named in the submitted paper's author header; it does not assert a current author employment relationship.
relation_types.released_by: The paper's official repository is owned by a reviewed lab or research organization.
relation_types.part_of: A reviewed research group-to-parent organization relationship.
relation_types.extends: The paper explicitly extends the target method.
relation_types.builds_on: The target method supplies a material starting point for the paper's design.
relation_types.uses_as_backbone: The paper explicitly uses the target as a backbone.
relation_types.adopts: The paper explicitly adopts a method or formalism from the target.
relation_types.adapts: The paper modifies a target method idea for a different setting or design.
relation_types.combines_with: The paper combines the target method with another material method component.
relation_types.adopts_component: The paper explicitly adopts a bounded component or preprocessing step.
relation_types.initializes_from: The target supplies an explicit initialization for the paper's representation or optimization.
relation_types.distills_from: The paper distills supervision, features, or priors from the target.
relation_types.uses_for_supervision: The paper uses the target to provide training or optimization supervision.
relation_types.uses_for_preprocessing: The paper uses the target for a material preprocessing or initialization stage.
relation_types.implementation_descends_from: The official implementation is author-asserted or verified as derived from the target paper's implementation.

2106.13228/source/files/02_related_work.tex § Neural Rendering: The most effective approach within this paradigm has been constructing a neural radiance field (NeRF) of a scene, and using a conventional multilayer perceptron (MLP) to parameterize volumetric density and color as a function of spatial scene coordinates~ [citation:mildenhall2020nerf] . NeRF's usage of classical volumetric rendering techniques has many benefits in addition to enabling photorealistic view synthesis: renderings from NeRF must correspond to a single coherent model of geometry, and the gradients of volumetric rendering are well-suited to gradient-based optimization.

edges.rationale: Retains: An MLP radiance field queried and volume-rendered along 3D camera rays. Changes: The template domain includes additional ambient coordinates selected per observation-space sample. Role: Provides the representation retained and modified by the target method.

2305.06356/source/files/sections/3_method.tex § Method: To enable efficient photo-realistic neural rendering of arbitrarily long multi-view data, we use sparse feature hash-grids in combination with shallow multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) [citation:mueller2022instant,SunSC22,hybrid_nerf] . The core idea of \methodname{} -- as illustrated in Fig.~ -- is to partition the time domain into optimally distributed temporal segments, and to represent each segment by a compact 4D feature grid (\S ). For this purpose, we propose an extension to the TensoRF vector-matrix decomposition of~ [citation:tensorf] -- designed for static 3D scenes -- that can support time-varying 4D feature grids.

edges.rationale: Retains: TensoRF vector-matrix decomposition. Changes: Extends the static decomposition to time-varying 4D feature grids with temporal segments. Role: 4D feature-grid representation.

edges.rationale: Retains: Colored 3D Gaussian primitives, splatting rasterization, and differentiable reconstruction. Changes: Adds temporally persistent position and orientation trajectories with physical motion regularizers. Role: Provides the Gaussian scene representation extended with persistent dynamic trajectories.

2310.08528/source/files/main.tex § Gaussian Deformation Field Network: To model 3D Gaussians' features effectively, we introduce an efficient spatial-temporal structure encoder $\mathcal{H}$ including a multi-resolution HexPlane $R(i,j)$ and a tiny MLP $\phi_d$ inspired by ~ [citation:tineuvox,hexplane,kplanes,tensor4d] . While the vanilla 4D neural voxel is memory-consuming, we adopt a 4D K-Planes~ [citation:kplanes] module to decompose the 4D neural voxel into 6 multi-resolution planes.

edges.rationale: Retains: The six-plane factorization and multiplicative interpolation used to decompose a 4D neural voxel. Changes: Queries the planes at Gaussian centers and decodes Gaussian deformation instead of radiance-field color and density. Role: Supplies the factorized spacetime feature encoder inside the Gaussian deformation field.

Gaussian Splatting represents a 3D scene explicitly with multiple Gaussian primitives, where the $i_{th}$ Gaussian primitive is parameterized by $\theta_i = (\mu_i, c_i, r_i, s_i, \sigma_i)$, where respectively represent the positions, color, rotation, scale, and opacity for the Gaussian primitive.

2505.08196/source/files/ijcai25.tex § Overview: To reconstruct any subsequent frame \(t = T\), we devise a coarse-to-fine strategy based on anchors. In the coarse stage, each anchor is deformed from the canonical space using lightweight multi-head MLPs, with the associated primitives subsequently updated based on the coarse deformation. In the fine stage, the opacity and color of each primitive are further refined using the deformed position of the anchors and current timestamp information. By combining both coarse and fine deformations, all deformed attributes of Gaussian primitives are obtained to render the current frame using volume splatting [citation:3dgs] .

2506.09518/source/files/4_method.tex § Induced Flow-Guided Deformation: Following the prior dynamic fusion methods~ [citation:sc-gs,dou2016fusion4d] , we adopt the linear blend skinning (LBS) strategy~ [citation:LBS] to compute the Gaussian deformation $\Delta x_j^t, \Delta r_j^t$ by interpolating the transformations of its neighboring anchors: \begin{equation} \Delta \mu_j ^t = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{A}_j} \omega_{ij} \left( \Delta R_i^t (\mu_j - x_i) + x_i + \Delta T_i^t \right), \quad \Delta r_j^t = \left( \sum_{i \in \mathcal{A}_j} \omega_{ij} \cdot \Delta R_i^t \right) \otimes r_j, \end{equation} where $\mu_j$ and $x_i$ denote the centers of Gaussian $j$ and anchor $i$, and $\otimes$ is quaternion multiplication.

2509.17864/source/files/tex/method.tex § Static and Dynamic Map Representation: We represent the scene map \(\mathcal{G} = \{\mathcal{G}_{\text{s}}, \mathcal{G}_{\text{d}}(t) \}\) as a set of 3D Gaussians~ [citation:kerbl20233d] , split into static \(\mathcal{G}_{\text{s}} = \{g_i\}_{i=1}^{N_s}\) and time-varying dynamic components \(\mathcal{G}_{\text{d}}(t) = \{g_i(t)\}_{i=1}^{N_d}\). 2605.22342/source/files/text/3_method.tex § Kinematic-Aware Joint Optimization: To prevent the watermark embedding degrading high-frequency structural details, we follow [citation:Jang_2025_CVPR] to adopt wavelet-subband loss $\mathcal{L}_{wav}$. This loss enforces consistency between the high-frequency coefficients of the watermarked image and the ground truth image $\mathcal{I}^{gt}$: \vspace{-2mm} \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal{L}_{wav} = \sum_{l} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{H}} \mathbb{E} \left[ \left\| \Phi_{s,l}(\hat{\mathcal{I}}^{t}_{v_j}) - \Phi_{s,l}(\mathcal{I}^{gt}) \right\|_1 \right], \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\Phi_{s,l}(\cdot)$ is the DWT coefficients in subband $s$ at decomposition level $l$.

edges.rationale: Retains: Wavelet-subband supervision that preserves high-frequency image structure. Changes: Kinematic gating and spatiotemporal consistency extend it to dynamic Gaussian assets. Role: Provides a mechanism that the target method explicitly adapts.

2607.21448/source/files/sections/method.tex § Canonical Anchor-Gaussian Scaffold: Following Scaffold-GS~ [citation:lu2024scaffoldgs] , we initialize anchor positions from the Structure-from-Motion (SfM) sparse point cloud, followed by voxel downsampling at resolution $v$ to obtain a spatially uniform anchor distribution.

2607.21448/source/files/sections/related_work.tex § Neural Scene Representations: 3D-GS~ [citation:kerbl2023threedgaussianspla] resolves this by representing scenes as anisotropic Gaussian primitives rendered via tile-based differentiable rasterization, achieving real-time performance while preserving competitive visual fidelity. Scaffold-GS~ [citation:lu2024scaffoldgs] introduced a hierarchical anchor structure in which neural Gaussians are spawned from sparse anchor points via learned offset MLPs, reducing redundant primitive proliferation and imposing structural regularity~ [citation:ren2025octreegs] .

edges.rationale: Retains: Sparse SfM-initialized anchors generate multiple child Gaussians from local offsets and anchor features. Changes: The scaffold is warmed up as a dynamic scene's canonical reference, then coupled to per-Gaussian deformation and temporal appearance branches. Role: representation
